detail.abstract: Bangladesh’s e-governance ecosystem, which has been built up over almost two decades on the back of the ‘Digital Bangladesh’ and ‘Smart Bangladesh’ visions, experienced a sudden political rupture with the fall of the Awami League government on 5 August 2024 and the installation of interim administration under Muhammad Yunus. This study conducts a qualitative analysis of the secondary-data of how that transition has impacted the institutional architecture of the digital governance of Bangladesh, processing the episode as a case of administrative continuity and disruption under political turbulence. The study conducted between August 2024 and 2026 draws on the public-administration theories of politico-administrative relations, bureaucratic continuity and institutional turbulence. It finds four interacting dimensions of change: (1) personnel and leadership disruption in flagship digital-governance institutions especially the Aspire to Innovate (a2i) programme; (2) symbolic and visionary discontinuity like the suspension of Smart Bangladesh Day and reframing of the long-term digital vision; (3) rapid, contested legal-regulatory reconstruction including repeal of the Cyber Security Act 2023 and drafting of the Cyber Security Ordinance 2025 and the Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025; (4) underlying operational continuity in the infrastructure for routine service delivery like the Union Digital Centres, e-Government Procurement, and e-Filing (Nothi), which remained mostly unchanged by the political change. According to the findings, Bangladesh’s digital governance transition, which will take place after August 2024, may best described not merely as the total collapse of the past regime, or continuation of the regime, but a layered pattern wherein overt, politically salient institutions suffered contested disruption while embedded operational systems displayed administrative continuity.  The manuscript advances knowledge, while also offering lessons for practice, of how to try to secure continuity in digital governance in times of political change.

detail.abstract: The Fiscal-Financial Temporal Entropy Index (FFTEI) theoretical framework identifies a structural failure mode called the Deferred Stability Illusion (DSI): a state in which headline stress indicators improve or stabilize while the underlying Risk Liquidation Base continues to expand, sustained by an active deferral mechanism. This paper provides the first empirical application of the DSI identification protocol to a specific, dateable policy event: the Federal Reserve's termination of quantitative tightening in December 2025 and its transition to full balance-sheet reinvestment. We demonstrate that all three DSI identification conditions were simultaneously satisfied at that juncture. Condition 1 (headline stability): SOFR held within approximately ten basis points of the federal funds rate midpoint throughout the transition period, and standing repo facility usage remained negligible. Condition 2 (expanding risk liquidation base): net federal interest expense reached a post-WWII record of 3.2 percent of GDP in FY 2025, or $970 billion, and the Congressional Budget Office projects further acceleration to 3.3 percent ($1.0 trillion) in FY 2026 and 4.6 percent by 2036. Condition 3 (active deferral mechanism): the FOMC's October 2025 announcement of full reinvestment directly expanded the deferred buffer B_T by committing future balance-sheet capacity to absorb Treasury supply. The concurrent discussion of collateraleligibility reform under Vice Chair Bowman introduces a structurally compounding element through the Collateral Swap mechanism, which FFTEI characterizes as irreversible. We propose four publicly observable proxy variables for real-time DSI tracking and derive a falsifiable prediction: if net interest expense as a share of GDP continues to rise over the subsequent four quarters while standard funding-stress measures remain subdued, the DSI hypothesis receives positive empirical support.

title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of the Oriented Ramsey Value k(3, 4) = 21

detail.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof of the Oriented Ramsey Value k(3, 4) = 21

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Let $k(3,4)$ denote the least positive integer $N$ such that every loopless oriented graph on $N$ vertices contains either an independent set of order three or a complete transitive tournament of order four. We give a computer-assisted proof that $k(3,4)=21$. A previously recorded cyclic oriented graph provides the lower bound. For the upper bound, elementary neighbourhood restrictions and an odd-order parity argument reduce any hypothetical counterexample on 21 vertices to 129 template cases. Eight certified classification refutations establish coverage of the required local templates. A further 108 certified refutations, together with 21 explicit transports under global arc reversal, exclude all remaining cases. The certificates are replayed using a strengthened LRAT checker after an independent computational audit identified a soundness defect in the originally deposited checker that could permit acceptance of an unsupported empty clause. The corrected checker rejects appropriate negative controls and successfully replays the complete selected certificate corpus. The result retains the ordinary trust boundary of the encoding, checker implementation, compiler, and execution platform; it is not a proof-assistant formalization. We make no priority claim over an earlier assertion of the same value.

title: The Dog That Didn't Bark: Tourism Dependence and the Pricing of Sovereign Credit Risk in Emerging Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Dog That Didn't Bark: Tourism Dependence and the Pricing of Sovereign Credit Risk in Emerging Markets
detail.abstract: Sovereign credit markets are assumed to price sectoral export concentration as a structural vulnerability. We test this premise using COVID-19—the largest tourism shock in history—as a natural experiment across 17 emerging markets. Our robust finding overturns conventional wisdom: the most tourism-dependent sovereigns experienced no differential CDS widening and no rating penalties during the shock. Institutional buffers—EU anchoring and IMF arrangements—completely suppress the sectoral signal. Yet pricing is not absent but delayed: tourism-exposed spreads normalized significantly more slowly, revealing that concentration risk surfaces in recovery dynamics rather than at impact. These findings challenge the view that export concentration commands a risk premium, identify official financing architecture as a first-order moderator of sovereign credit risk, and carry implications for precautionary instrument design in tourism-dependent economies.

detail.abstract: Competitive markets for perishable capacity (restaurants, hotels, airlines, appointment services) commit supply before stochastic demand realizes, and unused capacity expires. We study such markets through the operating frontier : the lowest zero-rent full price that supports a given participation level, indexed by a perishability parameter φ ∈ [0, 1] nesting the Walrasian benchmark (φ = 0). Three results follow. First, a distribution-free granularity principle: any convexorder increase in normalized demand dispersion raises the frontier. Second, participation-closed pass-through: cost shocks overshift the static benchmark 1+φW/Y (where W is expected unused capacity and Y is expected sales) even at zero profit, and compound in thin markets. Third, a de-pooling externality: entry that fragments demand across separately committed providers raises the frontier and can lower consumer surplus. Because the zero-rent frontier already carries the markup p-c = cφW/Y , high, rising, or countercyclical markups and above-one pass-through need not indicate market power.

During these episodes, robust private consumption, backed by expanding household purchasing power, coincided with greater pass-through of cost-push pressures into consumer prices. In particular, when core inflation rises above the mid-2% range, the similarity of price movements across individual items rises sharply, significantly raising the likelihood of price increases spilling over across a broader range of goods and services. detail.abstract: While intellectual property rights are intended to promote innovation and creativity, the current IPR system poses a significant barrier to the right to repair. There is an active discussion in IPR research on how to dismantle these barriers, and widespread support exists for actions that promote environmental sustainability. However, no significant steps have been taken in Europe to remove these barriers. This chapter investigates the reasons behind this lack of responsiveness particularly from EU perspective. These reasons are categorized into two groups: 1) Practical, surface level reasons such as the environmental sustainability focused aims of the right to repair in Europe, the top-down approach, siloed decision making structure of the European Commission and the difficulties to implement IPR related reforms combined with the decision making structure of the EU and 2) Deeper level reasons such as the architecture of IPRs in civil law system, the stronger natural law and personality based roots in Europe leading to focusing less on overall societal utility, and the strong semantic power of the “property” metaphor of IPRs leading to over-emphasis of the preservation of the status quo of the IPR landscape. These interconnected and mutually reinforcing issues hinder integration of right to repair into IPR systems. They together, to use a metaphor, form a human made “nylon wall” - a porous one but nevertheless a wall – between EU intellectual property and right to repair.

detail.abstract: India's approach to artificial intelligence governance is commonly discussed as a single national condition, obscuring substantial variation in readiness across the country's 36 states and Union Territories. This paper introduces the AI Governance Readiness Index (AIGRI), the first composite, multi-dimensional measure of AI governance readiness constructed at the state level for India. Built from six original datasets spanning digital infrastructure, institutional governance quality, innovation capacity, welfare delivery performance, digital safety, literacy, and AI policy activity, the Index ranks all 36 states and Union Territories and classifies them into four readiness tiers. Tamil Nadu ranks first (66.7) and Bihar last (28.9), isolated well below every other state. Telangana's maximum AI policy score alongside only a mid-tier overall rank demonstrates that published AI strategies do not equate to demonstrated governance capacity. A test of the relationship between readiness and welfare delivery outcomes finds only a weak, statistically insignificant correlation (r = 0.321, p = 0.056), indicating that general readiness gains will not resolve welfare-specific accountability failures. detail.abstract: Do governments react to the accumulation of public debt, ruling out fiscal unsustainability? As debt has massively increased to counter global financial and pandemic crises, this is a renewed pressing question for public policy analysis in an increasingly interconnected world economy. We examine budget data for a balanced panel of 52 industrial and emerging market economies over 1990–2024, employing the dynamic common correlated effects mean group estimator to account for global interdependencies and heterogeneous fiscal policy conduct. We show that an inertial primary-balance feedback policy rule  incorporating tax-smoothing objectives and explicitly responding to changes in outstanding debt has robust explanatory power in describing fiscal policymakers’ behavior across countries. Controlling for temporary output, temporary spending, and the current account balance, fiscal retrenchment exhibits a long-run upward adjustment in the primary surplus-GDP ratio by 0.86 percentage points on average per 10-percentage-point increase in the debt-GDP ratio. The positive fiscal reaction remains significant across high- and low-debt countries and across advanced and emerging economies. A comprehensive battery of robustness checks—including Covid-19 dummies, panel structural break tests, instrumental variable estimation, bias-corrected dynamic estimators, threshold regressions, piecewise splines, panel quantile regressions, and alternative detrending methods—confirms the stability of the results across all specifications. Despite heterogeneous fiscal responses, the evidence strongly indicates that most governments in both advanced and emerging economies do not engage in Ponzi-type financing and satisfy the intertemporal budget constraint through the systematic application of corrective fiscal policy, consistent with Ricardian fiscal behavior.

detail.abstract: Two topics have been studied separately: BIPV and phase-change material (PCM) thermal storage, but whether short-term weather uncertainty warrants, in real time, immediate use of available solar energy, its thermal storage, or its storage for reduced use during the cooling peak is still an unresolved coordinating question and not a solved one. This paper proposes a physics-based computational framework that couples a lumped-parameter RC building thermal model, standard PV performance model, enthalpy-method PCM phase-change model with a disclosed weather-forecast-driven rule-based predictive coordination algorithm for four control configurations (E0 conventional, E1 BIPV-only, E2 BIPV with passive PCM, E3 BIPV with PCM and predictive coordination) and four weather days (clear, cloudy, intermittent-solar, heatwave). On the clear days when the PV module is idle for most of the afternoon, as well as the intermittent days, the absolute peak grid import is reduced by up to 33% by implementing predictive coordination (E3: 1.01 and 0.98 kW respectively) compared to passive PV+PCM operation (E2: 1.49 and 1.25–1.31 kW respectively), although on the heatwave day, when the cooling system runs at its capacity ceiling for most of the day, predictive coordination increases the absolute peak by a maximum of 12.5% (E3: 1.01 kW against E2: 0.98 kW). A dedicated four-hour grid-outage stress test demonstrates a slight but notable passive-resilience benefit, in addition to the grid-connected peak-shaving benefit: PCM-equipped configurations (E2, E3) achieved a peak indoor temperature of 31.8 °C, compared to 32.6 °C for non-PCM configurations. A sensitivity analysis confirms that, among BIPV installations, the area of the PV panels is the most relevant lever for self-consumption. At the same time, the mass of PCM has a secondary impact, and, in the case of heatwaves in particular, the uncertainty in the forecast and the resistance of the envelope have a negligible marginal effect, as the decision threshold, already quite low, is largely surpassed by realistic forecast errors. It is an explicit statement in all these places that this is a numerical simulation Study, not a physical test-cell construction and monitoring programmed, and that we have a physics-based forward model that we know we can trust — and that we have described it — versus actual measurements of the irradiance, power, or indoor-temperature data, which would need to be collected in a physical test-cell before any deployment of the control strategy could inform us.

detail.abstract: Today, the transportation sector is a major contributor to greenhouse gas emissions and global warming. Accounting for approximately 14% of global fossil fuel consumption, it poses a significant challenge to sustainable development. In response, sustainable transportation has emerged as a key application of the sustainable development paradigm. Among its various modes, active transportation is particularly important because it relies on human physical activity for mobility and requires no direct fossil fuel consumption for propulsion during travel. Despite its environmental and public health benefits, active transportation adoption among Tehran’s citizens remains limited. Therefore, this study analyzes the causal relationships and degrees of influence exerted and influence received among key factors affecting citizens’ willingness to adopt active transportation. Specifically, it identifies the causal roles of these factors within the causal structure of active transportation adoption.,Using the Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (FDEMATEL) method and expert judgments, 30 indicators representing the environmental, social, and economic dimensions of sustainability were evaluated to determine their mutual influences and causal structure. The results show that all environmental indicators, together with 70% of social and economic indicators, belong to the cause group and serve as primary driving factors promoting citizens' willingness to use active transportation in Tehran. In total, 172 causal relationships were identified. Social, economic, and environmental dimensions ranked first, second, and third, with 67, 55, and 50 causal relationships, respectively. These findings provide an empirical basis for policies promoting active transportation adoption in Tehran.

detail.abstract:
India's urban development has reached an exciting milestone as Ahmedabad prepares to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and spearheads a prospective 2036 Olympic bid. These mega-events present a historic opportunity to accelerate world-class infrastructure while showcasing India’s commitment to equitable urban growth. To avoid the displacement challenges experienced during the 2010 Delhi Games, Ahmedabad has proactively utilized a refined land readjustment model via Town Planning Schemes (TPS) under the GTPUDA of 1976. While this approach successfully moves away from coercive eminent domain and minimizes legal gridlock, an opportunity exists to further protect informal tenants, landless laborers, and agrarian communities to ensure development is truly comprehensive. Currently, delegating planning to Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) ensures financial viability through land value capture, but this can be thoughtfully balanced with stronger social equity goals and safeguards.  

To maximize the positive social legacy of these historic events, this policy brief encourages a proactive shift towards a "Just Urbanism" framework by adapting the globally recognized Participatory and Inclusive Land Readjustment (PILAR) model.  The brief recommends establishing a collaborative CWG Olympic Land Covenant (COLC) to guide sustainable, community-focused development:  
- PILAR Institutionalization: Enhancing the existing TPS process by ensuring Local Stakeholder Committees include at least 33% non-title holders, fostering greater community consensus.  
- Social Tenure Domain Model (STDM): Utilizing advanced mapping of informal labor and tenancy ties to guarantee comprehensive and fair displacement allowances.  
- Inclusive Rehousing: Committing to collaborative rehabilitation practices that guarantee vulnerable families receive permanent, habitable in-situ housing.  
PDF
- Legacy Dividend Fund: Strategically reinvesting 20 percent of land auction revenues to directly fund affordable housing and stimulate local livelihoods.  


By embracing these inclusive, forward-thinking strategies alongside transparent social auditing, the government can set a pioneering global standard, ensuring Ahmedabad’s mega-events deliver a profound public good and a legacy of collaborative urban development.

detail.abstract: Injury severity in traffic accidents is influenced not only by the circumstances of individual events but also by the surrounding road network. However, whether traffic, weather, and roadway factors show consistent associations with injury outcomes across different network density conditions remains unclear. To address this issue, this research integrates road network information, traffic accident records, detector observations, and meteorological measurements from Northern California between 2019 and 2023. Five multi-year structural indicators were constructed for 467 spatial units centered on Caltrans Performance Measurement System (PeMS) detectors. Principal component analysis (PCA) summarized network structure, followed by multi-method consensus clustering to distinguish Low, Medium, and High road network density classes. The severity analysis covered 8,336 traffic accidents involving injury, each linked to traffic conditions during the preceding 30 min and concurrent weather observations. Ordered Logit (OL) or mixed ordered Logit (MOL) models were estimated separately for the three classes, and average marginal effects (AMEs) were evaluated on a common reference sample to ensure comparability. The combined proportions of severe and fatal outcomes were 18.6%, 13.0%, and 8.7% in the Low, Medium, and High classes, respectively. Cross-class tests identified 14 combinations of explanatory variables and severity levels with significant heterogeneity, corresponding to 23 significant pairwise differences and seven reversals in effect direction. The clearest differences involved lighting, road surface condition, construction or restriction status, and mean traffic flow. These findings indicate that increasing road network density does not produce a simple monotonic change in injury severity associations. Accounting for road network context can therefore support more targeted safety monitoring, risk warning, and intervention design.

This essay, part of a symposium on New Natural Law and analytical Thomism, studies how teleological analytical methods have enriched analytical jurisprudence. Those “analytical Aristotelian” methods have inspired two promising arguments in support of the natural law thesis. The legal point of view argument holds that law cannot be analyzed adequately except from the viewpoint of the wise statesman. That argument relies on Aristotle’s strategy of definition with central cases. The artifact argument holds that law has the same basic structure as other artifact-kinds and that its most important feature is its function, its promoting the common good by general and impersonal rule. That argument relies on Aristotle’s four-cause teleological framework. 

This essay summarizes the artifact and legal point of view arguments, and it identifies the Aristotelian features in both. The essay also explains the comparative advantages of each argument in analytical natural law theory. The artifact argument makes claims about law’s necessary features, while the legal point of view argument addresses methodological questions about how those features should be picked out. As made to date, however, neither argument addresses another preoccupation of analytical philosophy, explaining how shared concepts shape lay people’s social instincts in practice.

The key financial cost metric emerging from our framework is the Levelized Cost of CDR (LCCDR). detail.abstract: This study examines the development and intellectual evolution of behavioral finance research published in the Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance (JBEF) since its establishment. The objective is to identify the journal’s major publication trends, influential research areas, methodological preferences, and emerging themes that have shaped behavioral perspectives in finance. To achieve this objective, bibliometric and content analyses were conducted using the articles published in JBEF during its first eight years, with particular attention given to publication patterns, citation activity, contributing countries and institutions, theoretical foundations, research methods, and author keywords. The findings indicate that, despite its relatively short publication history, JBEF has achieved substantial scholarly visibility through a growing number of publications and citations. The United States represents a major source of research contributions, while Macquarie University and the University of Innsbruck emerge among the prominent institutional contributors. The analysis further shows that prospect theory and behavioral theory provide important conceptual foundations for much of the journal’s research. Quantitative approaches, archival datasets, and regression-based techniques are also widely employed. Eight major intellectual themes are identified, covering individual characteristics and national culture, psychological influences and financial literacy, investor sentiment and market volatility, experimental asset markets, overconfidence and disposition effects, COVID-19 and financial markets, socially responsible investment, and herding behavior. Overall, the study demonstrates the broadening scope of behavioral finance research and provides a structured overview of JBEF’s scholarly contributions, offering useful insights into established themes and potential directions for future research.

detail.abstract: Weitzman (1998) showed that recombining ideas makes new ideas superabundant, so ideas should never run scarce; yet measured productivity keeps falling. Full-recombinant growth assumes every successful invention becomes reusable material for future invention. We test that assumption directly, building the first invention-level genealogy of technology: 11,207 dated inventions joined by 4,735 dependencies. Only 16.9% of documented inventions have a descendant, and the number of descendants among those that do is so heavy-tailed that its variance is infinite. The genealogy rejects the full-recombinant benchmark in levels and reveals a highly unequal reproductive structure among successful innovations, an architecture we call semi-recombinant growth: only a measured subset of innovations become seeds for future invention, what we call innovation fertility. What remains open is direction: whether that fertile subset shrinks or grows with the stock of reusable knowledge. Our point estimate of this elasticity is negative, fertility rising rather than falling, but it is imprecise, sensitive to sourcing, and conflates two margins, becoming a seed at all and how prolific a seed is, that cannot currently be separated at this corpus’s scale; we report it as an open question, not a finding. Independently, under the model’s constant-elasticity benchmark, the seed value an invention carries is a distortion the market never prices, distinct from standard appropriability; identified from aggregate growth rates alone, it implies research effort should run about twenty-six percent higher than appropriability concerns alone would prescribe at postwar G7 values.

We study US transportation infrastructure on two asset classes: roadways, using 20,788 roughness spells on 2,549 FHWA Long-Term Pavement Performance (LTPP) sections matched to MERRA-2 climate-the first estimate of a climate-deterioration gradient from directly measured asset condition-and bridges, using 1.3 million inspection spells on 380,057 National Bridge Inventory (NBI) structures. Two-way fixed-effects estimates identify two opposing channels: summer heat raises annual roughness growth (0.0034 m/km per • C, p = 0.005), while freezing degree-days also damage pavement (4.1 × 10-5 per degree-day, t = 4.1), so warming relieves cold regions. At +2 • C, state effects run from-39% (Alaska) to +17% (Florida), and the national sign is a weighting question: equal-area averaging yields-4.8%, but lane-mile weighting flips the net to a cost of +1.6% (+4.1% VMT-weighted)-roughly +$0.15 to +$0.5 bn/yr under polar policy bounds, with confidence intervals that include zero and a net cost that grows convexly with warming depth as the freeze stock depletes. The bridge evidence delivers a complementary methodological result: NBI condition ratings improve with climate exposure-upgrades rise and downgrades fall where exposure is high-identifying the maintenance response rather than the physics, and showing why damage functions require measured physical outcomes like LTPP roughness. The robust objects are the fifty-point state gradient and the compositional flip: warming redistributes deterioration from the Frost Belt, where the network is sparse, to the Sun Belt, where the lane-miles and traffic are.

detail.abstract: The legality of the structure of variable interest entity (VIE) has long been a subject of contention since it was first used by Chinese companies to get listed overseas in the early 2000s. The VIE structure allows foreign investors to participate in overseas-listed Chinese companies through contractual control rather than a shareholding relationship, thus bypassing relevant restrictions on foreign investment in China. This paper argues that China adopts a policy of strategic ambiguity about the legality of the VIE structure, so as to balance the need to protect national security and the need to facilitate overseas listing of Chinese companies. There are institutional reasons behind this policy, including interest group politics of regulatory agencies and rent-seeking activities of regulatory officials. The policy of strategic ambiguity will likely continue in the foreseeable future, and so will the uncertainty over the legality of the VIE structure. However, the level of uncertainty is not as high as perceived by some commentators arguing that there is no law or legal protection for investors in the VIE market. This has important practical implications for the overseas listing of Chinese companies and foreign investors therein, as well as theoretical implications for the international discourse on law and finance.

detail.abstract: This paper reframes the standard-essential patent (SEP) licensing debate around structural holdout rather than holdup. detail.abstract: Manure application is a common agricultural practice with environmental and public health risks. detail.abstract: Households often respond little to news of a future cash transfer but increase spending sharply when the cash is received, generating an intertemporal kink in the cumulative spending response. This paper studies the mechanisms behind this pattern using survey experiments with liquid households in the United States and the United Kingdom. I show that the aggregate kink is driven primarily by households whose spending response is fully muted before receipt but rises sharply at receipt. Among these households, perceived uncertainty about the future payment is the most frequently cited reason for waiting. Experimental variation in control over future income shows that households are substantially more likely to choose a larger, delayed payment over a smaller, immediate payment when the delayed funds are placed in their own time-lock safe than when the same funds are guaranteed for future receipt but remain outside their control. Consistent with this mechanism, placing anticipated income in a time-locked setting reduces delayed spending and attenuates the kink. The results suggest that future income is less spendable before receipt because it is perceived as uncertain and weakly psychologically owned. I develop a two-account model in which perceived realization risk and incomplete psychological ownership limit discretionary spending against anticipated extra money, and calibrate it to the two U.S. experiments to reproduce the shift away from receipt-only spending to anticipatory spending.

detail.abstract: The Federal Reserve implements monetary policy using an ample reserves system, which does not require active management of the total quantity of reserves to maintain interest rate control. The distribution and the diffusion of reserves across banks, and groups of banks, is a key factor in determining the (minimum) ample level of reserves consistent with that objective. If large portions of the outstanding amount of reserves can become effectively "trapped" in segments of the banking system, then the total level of reserves needed to achieve the intended objective may be higher. We propose a Markovian framework to study the weekly flow of reserves across groups of banks between 2010 and 2024. We group banks according to types (foreign and domestic, large and small) and Fed districts. The diffusion process depends on how reserves flow in and out of the system. We compute counterfactuals which shed light on the way the distribution of reserves would adapt to plausible changes in conditions. In general, the distribution of reserves tends to be highly persistent during periods of abundant reserves, but redistribution intensifies when reserves reach lower (yet, still ample) levels.

detail.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive academic analysis of the systematic asset stripping and institutionalized corruption perpetrated by Sudan's National Islamic Front (NIF) and its successor, the National Congress Party (NCP), during their three-decade rule from 1989 to 2019. Central to this analysis is the regime's policy of tamkeen (empowerment)-a deliberate strategy through which regime loyalists penetrated state institutions, captured the economy, and systematically transferred public wealth to regime affiliates. Drawing upon the documented inventory of 63 state assets illicitly transferred during this period, alongside quantitative data from the World Bank and International Monetary Fund, this study examines the mechanisms, patterns, and consequences of what scholars have characterized as a kleptocratic system of governance. The analysis employs a multidisciplinary framework incorporating kleptocracy theory, state capture theory, and the political economy of authoritarianism to demonstrate how the NIF/NCP regime transformed the Sudanese state into an instrument of personal and factional enrichment. Through examination of banking sector privatization, agricultural scheme dispossession, infrastructure asset sales, and diplomatic property transfers, this paper argues that the regime's privatization policies constituted not genuine economic reform but rather systematic state capture enabled by the ideology of tamkeen. The findings reveal that privatization served as a vehicle for political patronage, that legal frameworks were deliberately manipulated to facilitate asset transfers to regime affiliates, and that the cumulative effect was the comprehensive dismantling of Sudan's public wealth. The paper concludes by examining post-2019 asset recovery efforts and considers the implications for transitional justice and economic reconstruction.

detail.abstract: This paper documents a sharp and persistent collapse of the hedonic size elasticity of housing prices in Istanbul at the December 2021 Turkish lira credibility shock. Using 414,819 sale and rental listings from January 2019 to February 2026, we estimate that the elasticity of price with respect to floor area fell by 0.165 (sales) and 0.169 (rentals) in central districts, with smaller but significant declines in peripheral districts. The break is precisely timed, absent at pre-treatment placebo dates, fully present against the pre-pandemic 2019 baseline, and strengthens in a fully interacted hedonic specification in which all attribute prices may change. We adjudicate among candidate explanations using cross-segment symmetry, regime chronology, regulation timing, and socioeconomic incidence. The distinctive predictions of the alternatives fail: there is no pandemic-era elasticity elevation to normalise from; the collapse appears fully within the pre-1999 building cohort that new supply cannot enter; the June 2022 rent regulation explains at most the post-regulation deepening of the central rental response; and the affordability signature (concentration of the collapse where budget constraints bind) is absent, with the rental incidence gradient running toward the most expensive neighbourhoods instead. The joint pattern is most consistent with scarcity repricing: a shift of the marginal bid toward locationally scarce units, operating alongside conventional asset-hedge demand. A collapse of monetary credibility restructures relative prices within an asset class, making the cross-sectional hedonic gradient a sensitive diagnostic of monetary regimes.​

detail.abstract: Attendance is the most elementary legislative behaviour and, in comparative work, a favoured measure of legislator effort. In Nigeria it is not merely understudied; it is largely unrecorded. This article examines the sitting record of a full session of the Nigerian Senate and reports a finding in two parts. detail.abstract:
A merger wave has swept across the wholesale electricity generation market, and the result is higher prices for consumers. Federal oversight of electricity mergers is meant to prevent this type of consolidation, but the system has failed. Congress has granted two agencies—the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, FERC, and the Antitrust Division of the Department of Justice—concurrent authority to review mergers among wholesale electricity suppliers. In theory, this dual merger review system should better advance competition by combining FERC’s deep knowledge of market structure with the Antitrust Division’s significant expertise in competition analysis.

This Article critically evaluates the current dual system of review and shows that it is broken. FERC evaluates the competitive effects of wholesale electricity mergers using a simple market-concentration screen, which the Article demonstrates can readily fail to identify anticompetitive mergers. Meanwhile, the Antitrust Division, despite employing economic tools better capable of identifying competitive harm, rarely challenges wholesale electricity mergers. The result is a perverse allocation of regulatory authority, where the agency with less merger review expertise and weaker analytic tools plays the greater role in determining which mergers are approved and on what terms.

 The Article proposes a different structure for electricity merger review. The Antitrust Division should be the sole agency tasked with assessing a merger’s effects on competition, while FERC’s review should focus on public interest concerns beyond competition. This approach better aligns each agency’s role with its expertise and would help protect consumers from wholesale electricity mergers that generate competitive harm.

detail.abstract: This chapter analyzes the evolving terrain of social license to operate (SLO) vis-a-vis the concentration of executive political power and the changing nature of environmental impact assessment (EIA) in Canada since Prime Minister Mark Carney’s 2025 election. We contribute to the debates on SLO by examining how Carney’s administration is altering the nation’s environmental governance framework, processes of Indigenous consultation, and subsequent project approval/permitting. We analyze public releases from the federal government, including two May 2026 discussion papers detailing how these legislative changes will be operationalized. We argue the Carney administration is using two strategies to rapidly advance extractive capitalist projects that strongly limit opposition: (1) the concentration of proposed development decision-making powers in the executive branch; (2) the alteration of federal EIA regulations to limit constitutional obligations to consult Indigenous peoples. Both strategies undermine democratic decision-making over development in Canada and disproportionately serve extractive industries, aided by a revolving door of industry elites into the newly created Major Projects Office (MPO). As mutually reinforcing and interdependent parts of the Carney Liberals’ governance approach, they are conditioned by financial and extractive capitalist need for profitability. In this shifting legislative landscape, we observe that, in contrast to predecessor PM Trudeau, SLO does not appear to be a priority for the current federal government.

detail.abstract: Are policies designed to alleviate firms' financing constraints an effective stabilization tool during non-financial crises? We combine survey data on firms' beliefs and investment plans with granular credit registry data (AnaCredit) and administrative records to show that these programs were poorly targeted. From the onset of COVID-19, most firms identified weak consumer demand and supply-chain disruptions, not access to finance, as their primary concerns. Moreover, among firms seeking external financing, most preferred conventional commercial loans, despite the availability of lower-rate guaranteed alternatives. Firms that relied on guaranteed loans were negatively selected, exhibiting zombie-like characteristics. Despite receiving support, these firms experienced relatively weaker post-pandemic fundamentals and were more likely to reduce their product prices, potentially generating disinflationary effects. Our findings underscore the value of incorporating firms' real-time assessments into the design of stabilization policies, rather than relying on out-of-context historical precedents.

title: Knowledge-Space Intelligence: A Geometric Framework for Reliable Decision Making under Knowledge-Definition Uncertainty
affiliations: Université de Moncton, Alfaisal University, University of Hail and Université de Moncton

detail.title: Knowledge-Space Intelligence: A Geometric Framework for Reliable Decision Making under Knowledge-Definition Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence traditionally assumes that reliable decisions emerge from sufficiently informative or identifiable representations of reality. However, numerous scientific and engineering problems admit multiple knowledge representations that are simultaneously consistent with the available evidence while leading to different interpretations of the underlying phenomenon. This paper introduces the concept of Knowledge-Definition Uncertainty, a form of uncertainty arising from ambiguity in the organization and interpretation of knowledge rather than from data noise, parameter estimation, or model uncertainty. To address this challenge, we propose Knowledge-Space Intelligence (KSI), a geometric framework in which intelligence operates over a structured space of admissible knowledge states instead of a single latent representation. Each admissible knowledge state induces a corresponding decision landscape, transforming intelligent decision making into the search for decisions that remain stable across competing yet defensible interpretations of reality. The proposed framework introduces formal notions of knowledge spaces, knowledge geometry, decision landscapes, and knowledge equilibrium, establishing a variational perspective for trustworthy artificial intelligence under ambiguous knowledge. Unlike existing approaches that optimize over feature spaces or model parameters, KSI optimizes over admissible knowledge representations, providing a principled mathematical foundation for reliable decision making under structural ambiguity. The framework naturally extends reliability-aware artificial intelligence and provides a theoretical basis for future developments within the Unified Variational Intelligence Framework (UVIF), where knowledge itself becomes an optimization variable. Potential applications include scientific discovery, autonomous systems, foundation models, medical diagnosis, and other domains in which multiple coherent interpretations of reality coexist.

detail.abstract: Global current-account imbalances narrowed when the exceptional pandemic and energy-price shocks receded, then widened again in 2024-2025. This paper examines the implications for equilibrium exchange rates with a two-level fundamental equilibrium exchange rate model through 2026. Estimated medium-run current-account norms are combined with a six-bloc world trade system and national euro-area models. The evidence identifies a renewed US-China fault line. In the provisional 2025 estimates, China is undervalued by 26.6 log percentage points in real-effective terms and the United States is overvalued by 24.3; the conditional 2026 gaps remain 23.7 and 22.0, respectively. The direction and approximate magnitude accord with the IMF's 2025 external assessments. The underlying imbalance reflects weak US public saving alongside high Chinese saving and subdued domestic absorption. Dollar dominance, balance-sheet effects, and geopolitical fragmentation influence the speed and distribution of adjustment. Durable rebalancing calls for credible fiscal consolidation in the United States, consumption-enhancing reform and greater exchange-rate flexibility in China, stronger productive demand elsewhere, and restraint in using tariffs as a current-account instrument.

detail.abstract:
Background: Community-based health insurance (CBHI) aims to extend health coverage to informal-sector and vulnerable populations in low- and middle-income countries, but greater enrolment might not translate into effective and equitable coverage. We examined how subsidies and CBHI operational capacity were associated with enrolment, healthcare use, catastrophic health expenditure (CHE), and socioeconomic equity. 

Methods: We linked representative household surveys from 2019 and 2022 with census surveys of CBHI schemes from 2017 and 2020 across three regions of Senegal. We compared partially and fully subsidised CBHI models on enrolment, healthcare utilization, and CHE, examined associations with scheme operational capacity, and assessed socioeconomic inequalities using slope and relative inequality indices. 

Findings: The surveys included 1,767 households in 2019 and 2,160 households in 2022. Enrolment among those eligible for fully subsidised CBHI increased from 17·4% to 38·5%, while enrolment in the partially subsidised population remained below 3%. Enrolment was associated with greater healthcare utilization in the partially subsidised population (OR 1·63, 95% CI 1·25-2·13), but not among those eligible for full subsidies (1·19, 0·82–1·74), and was not associated with lower CHE in either population. Associations between scheme operational-capacity indicators and outcomes were heterogeneous. Enrolment was pro-rich under both models; among those eligible for full subsidies, the slope index of inequality was 10·3 percentage points (95% CI 2·9-17·7) in 2019 and 13·4 (4·2-22·6) in 2022. 

Interpretation: Enrolment expanded substantially among those eligible for fully subsidised CBHI, but this expansion was not accompanied by consistent evidence of greater healthcare use or financial risk protection, and socioeconomic inequalities in enrolment persisted. Associations with scheme operational capacity were heterogeneous, suggesting that scheme-level strengthening alone might be insufficient. Achieving effective and equitable coverage might require broader financing and risk-pooling reforms alongside interventions addressing non-financial barriers to enrolment and care.

title: Hospital Closures and the Evolution of the Health Care Establishment Landscape in Rural America

detail.title: Hospital Closures and the Evolution of the Health Care Establishment Landscape in Rural America
detail.abstract: Rural hospital closures and threats to the viability of remaining hospitals continue to raise concerns about access to health care in rural America. Yet, we lack evidence on the evolution of the local health care establishment landscape following a closure. We use restricted-use Longitudinal Business Database data to estimate the causal effect of hospital closures on the number of establishments and employment across different types of health care services. We can rule out even small decreases in non-hospital health care establishments and find an immediate increase in non-hospital health care employment equal to 25 to 42% of the decrease in hospital employment. Extensive and intensive increases occur in home health services, dialysis centers, and physician offices. While communities leverage closures into some restructuring of health care services, they almost certainly lead to a net loss of services. Further, substitution towards outpatient care occurs only in counties with remaining hospitals.​

detail.abstract: Public moral discourse assumes that the willingness to help is limitless. That assumption is wrong. Goodwill is finite, vulnerable to depletion, and highly dependent on feedback: repeated overload, coercion, fraud, or visible ineffectiveness can make otherwise prosocial actors reduce future helping. This paper develops a middle-range framework of bounded altruism to explain how societies can protect and reproduce goodwill rather than merely demand more of it. The framework identifies three conditions for sustainable helping: capacity (the helper can bear the cost without serious damage to basic obligations and longterm functioning), authenticity (the need is genuine and the form of assistance matches it), and voluntariness (help remains a chosen contribution rather than an ordinary duty enforced through shame). These conditions are embedded in a feedback process in which helping outcomes, recognition, trust, and institutional protection update the actor's willingness to help again. The paper then adds a fourth mechanism-generalized reciprocity. Gratitude should not convert assistance into a private debt owed to the original helper; at its best, it becomes a willingness to carry goodwill forward when one later becomes able to help another. On this basis, moral governance is reconceived as the protection, circulation, and social reproduction of goodwill. Illustrative Chinese cases show how excessive moral benchmarking and weak signal screening can deplete the willingness to help. Confucian and Daoist resources are read not as a civilizational alternative to Western theory, but as locally resonant insights: support the giver and restrain coercion. The paper concludes with an educational and institutional agenda for cultivating sustainable prosocial character-cost awareness, proportionality, capacity-sensitive giving, gratitude, and pay-it-forward reciprocity. The central claim is simple: goodwill is too valuable to be spent carelessly.

detail.abstract: We examine auditors’ role in diffusing forecasting knowledge among their clients. We hypothesize that auditors share forecasting process knowledge and best practices across clients, which improves management forecast accuracy. We find that companies forecast more accurately when their auditors have greater exposure to forecasting knowledge through other clients, consistent with forecasting knowledge diffusion through auditors. This association between auditor forecasting knowledge and management forecast accuracy is greater when managers (a) face more dynamic difficult-to-forecast environments, (b) have less skill and resources, and (c) have fewer alternative forecasting information sources. However, auditor forecasting knowledge is not associated with audit quality or auditor independence concerns, consistent with auditors affecting management forecasting through a knowledge sharing process unrelated to governance. Our results persist through multiple robustness tests, including an instrumental variable regression and selection models. Our research indicates a novel source of valuable knowledge that clients obtain from auditor knowledge sharing which improves clients’ unaudited information environment.

detail.abstract: For the two-stage adaptive robust linear program with uncertain right-hand side b in U (m-dimensional, nonnegative orthant), Bertsimas and Goyal (2012) prove that affine decision rules are optimal when U is a simplex of m+1 vertices and that when U has m+3 vertices (two beyond a simplex), the affine cost can exceed the fully-adaptive cost by a factor arbitrarily close to 2. The intermediate case of m+2 vertices (one beyond a simplex) is settled by neither result. We settle it negatively in this paper. An explicit all-integral instance in dimension m=2 with U the convex hull of the origin and three nonzero vertices (m+2=4 in total) has fully-adaptive value 1 but affine value 12/11, a gap of 1/11. The lower bound is a Farkas certificate and the upper bound is an explicit affine decision rule. A block-diagonal construction gives the same gap in every dimension m>=2 with exactly m+2 vertices. Thus the simplex bound is sharp: affine optimality cannot be extended one vertex beyond a simplex. The arguments use only linear programming duality and are verifiable by hand.

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces the Community Mobility Framework™, a developmental framework describing how lived experience may progress through recognition, translation, activation, community contribution, and generational legacy. Rather than viewing individuals primarily through deficits or service needs, the framework positions experiential knowledge as a potential community asset capable of strengthening leadership, workforce participation, civic engagement, and intergenerational knowledge preservation. detail.abstract: In recent years, the advent of increasingly connected medical devices, from wearable biosensors to even implantable diagnostic devices, has created an unprecedented amount of clinically valuable data, but regulatory, ethical and technical hurdles remain to enable such data to be combined for the training of robust artificial intelligence models. To mitigate this, federated learning (FL) is proposed, which trains models in a federated way with no centralization of raw patient records, but existing federated learning architectures suffer from relying entirely on a central orchestrating server, leading to the existence of a single point of failure, poor auditability, and vulnerable to poisoning and free-riding attacks. This review presents a systematic literature survey and analysis of blockchainbased federated learning for healthcare, and explores how these two fundamentally different approaches can be brought together to create a secure, auditable and trustworthy orchestration layer that enables medical intelligence to be built across multiple devices and to incorporate privacy-preserving approaches such as data aggregation, differential private tools and secure multiparty calculations. The review is based on over 40 peer-review, published papers mainly focused on the period from 2019 to 2025, and is summarised in four core tiers of reference architecture, with consensus mechanisms identified as appropriate for resource-constrained clinical devices, and energy usage and model utility trends highlighted. It continues to discuss the scalability and regulatory challenges in participation with regulations like General Data Protection Regulation and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, the heterogeneity of the model for non-independent and identically distributed clinical datasets and the computational complexity of blockchain consensus mechanisms on hardware with limited capability. The review suggests blockchain-enabled federated learning is a technically feasible and increasingly proven route to intelligent health applications in networked environments that do not compromise patient privacy, but points to a need for simplified consensus mechanisms, interoperable learning protocols, and greater partnerships with healthcare governance institutions.

detail.abstract: International logistics performance is often summarized through broad national rankings, even though operational bottlenecks can occur at very different points in a supply chain. This study uses the World Bank Logistics Performance Indicators 2.0 (LPI 2.0) to diagnose Bangladesh's international logistics performance using 2023 and 2024 shipment-based indicators. Seventeen indicators applicable to Bangladesh are examined across maritime, aviation, and postal logistics. Bangladesh is benchmarked against current World Bank South Asian economies and the World Bank lower-middle-income aggregate, using raw values, direction-adjusted gaps, regional ranks, year-toyear changes, and mean-median-interquartile-range diagnostics. The results show a mixed rather than uniformly weak logistics profile. In 2024, Bangladesh had 13 maritime partner countries, compared with 44.3 among South Asian peers excluding Bangladesh and 26.5 for lower-middle-income economies. B2B postal delivery averaged 16.9 days, also worse than both benchmarks. By contrast, container export dwell time was 1.8 days and import supply-chain termination time was 1.7 days, outperforming both comparison groups. From 2023 to 2024, maritime partner connectivity fell by 31.6%, while mean B2B and B2C postal delivery times rose by 42.0% and 81.7%, respectively. The B2C median remained broadly stable while dispersion widened, suggesting that the deterioration was concentrated in slower deliveries rather than being uniform. The findings indicate that Bangladesh's principal weaknesses lie in connectivity and selected reliability dimensions, not in every stage of international logistics. The study demonstrates the value of operational, indicator-level benchmarking for more targeted logistics policy and supply-chain decision making.

title: How to Forecast Non-Obvious Innovations

detail.abstract: Companies forecast innovation with instruments built for forecasting sales: they extrapolate the attribute the market rewards today and call the slope the future. This is pattern recognition, and pattern recognition reads frequency in a remembered series. It is silent exactly where innovation happens-at the jump, when a lighter embodiment dissolves an obligation buyers had stopped noticing, an event absent from any series because it has not yet happened. This paper proposes path recognition as the alternative operation: reading the dependency structure that holds an embodiment in place-its obligations, its identity chain, the capabilities that could change it-rather than the frequency of its past. The paper separates four words the roadmap conflates (forecast, prediction, expectation, desire), places eight established forecasting families on the map of what they read and what they output, and states plainly where a fat-tailed environment breaks each of them, drawing on Kahneman's account of the heuristics that generate pattern recognition and on Taleb's account of the tails that defeat it. It surveys how six other fields already forecast under related conditionsmeteorology, epidemiology, seismology, venture capital, military net assessment, and the deliberate culture-building studied in team research-and treats the innovating organisation as a system of stocks, flows and feedback, in the sense used in systems theory, so that an innovation jump becomes a leverage-point intervention rather than a parameter tweak. A specific model is proposed and specified for testing: four measurable variables, a coding protocol, a historical backtest and a prospective trial, each with a stated failure condition. Extreme counterfactuals are then run across five unrelated domains-telephony, books, drinking water, photography and home heating-to stress the model outside its country of origin, alongside three deeper company forecasts (Versuni, Apple, OpenAI), each with a jump, a set of directions to leave alone, a disappearance risk and a falsifier. The paper closes with the positioning dissection a company can run on itself, the forecast machine that runs it quarterly, and the limits of the whole claim. Every forecast produced here is a method-generated hypothesis; the tests, ahead of the argument, decide it.

detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how eco-anxiety shapes sustainable travel intention under hope-and doom-framed climate messages and whether it leads to different behavioural pathways, including sustainable intention, avoidance, or rationalisation. Methodology/Design/Approach: Based on the Somatic Marker Hypothesis and Prospect Theory, this research uses a rulebased affective-cognitive pathway simulation, survey-based hypothesis testing, and an integrative interpretation of the two analytical stages. The simulation phase profiles four plausible behavioural pathways: Green Shift, Rationalisation, Avoidance, and Neutral. A structured online survey was then used to test the hypotheses. Findings: Results showed that eco-anxiety was positively associated with sustainable travel intention and that this relationship was stronger under the assigned hope-framing condition than under the assigned doom-framing condition. Moderation analysis revealed selective contextual variation: region remained significant after adjustment for multiple testing, whereas the employment interaction was significant only at the unadjusted level. Risk perception did not mediate the eco-anxiety-intention relationship, indicating that this relationship was not explained by the measured risk-appraisal pathway. Originality of the research: The study positions eco-anxiety as a conditional affective signal and offers tourism managers and destination communicators a pathway-based basis for designing climate messages that support agency-oriented sustainable travel decisions.

detail.abstract:
Artificial-intelligence acceleration creates a governance problem that cannot be reduced to technical capability or institutional readiness alone. This paper develops Dynamic Civilizational Adaptation (DCA), a falsifiable systems architecture for studying bounded socio-technical decision systems under changing AI pressure. DCA models the relationship between technical pressure, context-specific required response capacity, persistent response-capacity gaps, absorption, task-relevant human capability, rights and actionability constraints, epistemic uncertainty, and the viability of future options. The framework explicitly separates improved technical or organizational throughput from retained human adaptive capacity and rejects compensatory aggregation where rights or actionability constraints fail.

The paper specifies a minimal estimable kernel, RBG-DCA-E1, and evaluates the architecture through two author-designed synthetic diagnostics: a 2026–2055 stress test and a post-specification model-recovery red team. The synthetic results are not empirical validation. Instead, they expose identification and complexity risks, including cases in which correlated states generate false structural inference, motivating model reduction and explicit kill conditions.

A nested candidate extension, DCA-RF, further asks whether persistent adaptation gaps can erode the feasible set of interventions capable of preserving or restoring a critical option, and whether minimum recovery burden can rise before contemporaneous performance visibly deteriorates. Recoverability, viability, path dependence, lock-in, absorptive capacity, human oversight, contestability, and related constructs are treated as established prior-art domains rather than individually novel concepts. The candidate contribution is therefore compositional and empirical: whether the specified coupling architecture provides reproducible incremental predictive, diagnostic, or decision value over stronger simpler baselines. The paper concludes with a preregistration-oriented Golden Case protocol and explicit criteria for narrowing, demoting, or killing unsupported components.

detail.abstract:
Reform of the global health architecture has moved from diffuse critique into formal multilateral process, yet analysis of that reform remains caught between diagnosis and prescription. This article develops and applies a two-level analytical framework. Its observational layer adapts the Governance Analytical Framework, which treats governance empirically—as interaction among actors around a public problem, producing decisions and social norms—rather than normatively. Its evaluative layer specifies eight architecture dimensions: governance legitimacy, health sovereignty, financing sustainability, equity, institutional coherence, accountability, country ownership, and resilience. The framework is applied to five initiatives selected for maximum variation in legal form and locus of authority: the WHO Pandemic Agreement, the 2024 amendments to the International Health Regulations, the Pandemic Fund, the Lusaka Agenda, and the Accra Reset, with Africa CDC treated as a regional scale that reconfigures rather than supplements the global question.

Drawing on scholarship on fragmentation, regime complexes, and orchestration, I define managed pluralism through four conditions—functional differentiation, interface institutionalisation, distributed accountability, and capability-directed financing—which distinguish governed diversity from both conflictive fragmentation and centralisation. No initiative resolves the architectural problem; the five occupy distinct and partly complementary niches, and coherence proves weakest precisely where authority is most binding. Applied to the present field, the four conditions return an unfavourable verdict, satisfied only partially and, in the case of interface institutionalisation, scarcely at all. The contribution is diagnostic and testable rather than prescriptive: the conditions generate falsifiable expectations, and the article specifies the observations that would disconfirm them and addresses the objection that managed pluralism risks legitimating donor-serving disorder.

detail.abstract: Mainstream assessments of artificial intelligence's labor-market effects rely on production-function models in which technology shifts the marginal products of capital and labor. Even sophisticated task-based variants, which represent automation and task reinstatement as a decentralized equilibrium outcome rather than a planner's assignment, cannot supply, once asked to calibrate a specific corrective policy, the boundary between automatable and non-automatable work, the pace of task reinstatement, or the other parameters that calibration requires. This paper argues, from within Austrian praxeology and heterogeneous capital theory, that such calibration requires dispersed, tacit knowledge generated only by the market process the policy would forestall-weaker than the common assertion that no policy could ever improve on inaction. Building on Frank Knight's risk/uncertainty distinction, large language models are classified as higher-order capital goods operating within a closed space of statistically weighted outcomes, incapable of the entrepreneurial function of forming new ends under uncertainty. The paper re-derives the transitional character of technological unemployment, Say's Law's compatibility with automation, the exposure of AI investment to interest-rate distortion, and the informational demands that make a precisely optimal automation tax uncomputable, while declining overstatements common in popular Austrian commentary: aggregate labor non-specificity differs from individual human-capital specificity, Lachmannian indeterminacy is a genuine constraint rather than an ornamental citation, and a Mengerian valuation premium on human-originated output cannot by itself reabsorb displaced labor at scale. The argument draws on historical and 2026 labor-market evidence, engages recent Austrian AI scholarship, and closes by confronting the framework's strongest objections.

detail.abstract:
Governments invest substantial public resources in research through investigator-led grants, mission programs, government laboratories, infrastructure, talent recruitment and tax incentives. Decisions combine scientific assessment, institutional mandates, political priorities, regional considerations and historical allocations. Yet governments lack a common framework for comparing the multiple forms of public impact research might produce, the processes required to realize them and the jurisdictions and populations in which benefits accrue. Inputs and intermediate outputs—including expenditure, publications, patents, licences, startups, venture capital and jobs—can consequently become substitutes for public impact.

This paper develops a process-informed Research-to-Public-Impact framework. Building on the reduced-form intuition that research can increase the frequency and potential magnitude of innovation, it distinguishes potential from realized impact and represents impact as a multidimensional vector. Realization depends on an iterative research-to-use process involving technology-use-user configuration, adoption, diffusion and productive use. Additionality establishes what changed because of public intervention; geographic incidence identifies where benefits accrue; and explicit priorities guide interpretation of plural public value.

The framework imports a total-quality perspective into research policy: a system cannot be improved systematically when its process is misunderstood and data capture only inputs and visible outputs. Pathway evidence about assumptions, rejection, redirection, implementation and use should therefore inform subsequent portfolio and support decisions. The equations provide a testable conceptual decomposition and decision aid—not a precise forecasting algorithm or a replacement for endogenous-growth theory. The aim is to improve realization yield, reduce avoidable conversion loss and generate greater public value from limited resources.

detail.abstract: A buyer who pays more than an earlier buyer for the same flight, hotel stay or event may perceive the difference as unfair, but the benchmark is a price the firm itself chose. This paper studies dynamic pricing when the comparison benchmark is endogenous to the seller's earlier pricing decision. Consumers evaluate later prices against an expectation reference determined in personal equilibrium and a comparison reference created by the firm's initial price. Expectationbased loss aversion smooths prices, while comparison-based inequity aversion compresses price differences across cohorts. Because the initial cohort creates the benchmark without itself facing an earlier-cohort comparison, the firm optimally raises the launch price above the static monopoly benchmark to relax future behavioural constraints. Stronger interpersonal comparisons therefore generate both higher launch prices and smaller subsequent price differences: under empirically plausible parameters the launch price rises by 5 to 10 per cent while cross-cohort dispersion falls by 80 to 95 per cent. The premium is bounded rather than escalating, rising with comparison intensity only up to a threshold beyond which the firm prices at the benchmark in every state. Extending the model to an arbitrary number of repricing epochs with finite capacity, the launch premium is strictly positive at every repricing frequency, and numerically it increases as the selling window is divided more finely and is largest at intermediate scarcity. Finer algorithmic repricing therefore magnifies rather than eliminates the distortion. Cohort comparison is a distinct intertemporal force in dynamic pricing, with implications for launch pricing and algorithmic pricing systems.

detail.abstract: Peer residential leaders occupy an unusual position within Australian residential colleges and university accommodation. They are students, neighbours, role models and community builders, yet they may also be expected to notice distress, respond to intoxication, manage conflict, enforce community standards, receive disclosures, support students after hours and connect residents with professional services. This conceptual article argues that these student leaders form a hidden frontline of student wellbeing. Their value lies precisely in their proximity: they see everyday changes in behaviour, belonging and functioning that formal services may never observe. Yet proximity also creates risk. When role expectations are unclear, peer leaders can experience boundary erosion, emotional labour, role conflict, burnout and secondary traumatic stress, while institutions may unintentionally shift professional responsibilities onto students. Drawing on higher education peer-support research, resident assistant scholarship, burnout and job demands-resources theory, mental health first-aid research and the contemporary Australian regulatory context, the paper develops a Supported Supporter Framework for residential education. The framework proposes six institutional commitments: role clarity; training for recognition, response and referral; reliable escalation architecture; active supervision and debriefing; protected boundaries around availability and responsibility; and explicit care for the wellbeing of peer leaders themselves. The article argues that peer leadership is most effective when it is neither romanticised as informal friendship nor professionalised beyond its limits. Residential colleges should design peer leadership as a supported relational role: close enough to notice, skilled enough to respond initially, and connected enough to transfer responsibility safely to professionals when the situation exceeds the peer role.

Purpose: This study examines how NFT design attributes, algorithmic rarity, visual characteristics and historical trading dynamics predict valuation and liquidity across different trading stages.

Design/methodology/approach: Using NFT transaction histories and NFT characteristics data for 126,513 tokens from ten leading profile photo NFT collections, the study applies an ensemble of five machine-learning models to predict primary/secondary sale prices and early/subsequent trading frequency. SHAP analysis is used to explain predictor importance.

Findings: NFT market outcomes are stage dependent. Rarity and visual attributes dominate primary pricing and early trading frequency, while historical trading dynamics become the strongest predictors of secondary prices and subsequent trading activity. Rarity is more influential than visual attributes for predicting prices, whereas visual attributes are more influential for predicting trading frequency.

Originality: The study integrates NFT collection design, rarity, visual attributes, and trading history within an explainable ensemble framework, demonstrating how their importance changes across NFT lifecycle stages.

detail.abstract: Student wellbeing and student conduct are commonly organised as separate domains within higher education. In Australian residential colleges, however, this distinction is often unstable in practice. Changes in engagement, repeated non-response, withdrawal from communal life, alcohol-related incidents, conflict, hostility, boundary breaches or apparent non-compliance may sometimes occur alongside psychological distress, trauma, adjustment difficulties or other forms of vulnerability. These behaviours are not diagnostic and should never be presumed to arise from distress. Yet treating them only as disciplinary problems can miss opportunities for early support, while treating them only as wellbeing matters can minimise harm, weaken accountability and compromise procedural fairness. This conceptual article examines the wellbeing-conduct nexus in Australian residential colleges and proposes a Care-Conduct Continuum for responding to behaviour that may carry both welfare and disciplinary significance. Drawing on Australian higher education regulation, student mental health research, trauma-informed practice, procedural justice and restorative justice scholarship, the article advances five connected practices: notice without diagnosis; engage before escalation; differentiate wellbeing, risk and conduct; respond with proportionate accountability; and repair, reintegrate and review. It argues that trauma-informed practice should shape how conduct processes are designed and experienced, but should not predetermine factual findings or remove responsibility for harm. The paper positions procedural fairness itself as a wellbeing-relevant practice and concludes that residential colleges are particularly well placed to develop integrated models because they combine proximity, community, pastoral support and behavioural governance. The central challenge is not to choose between care and accountability, but to learn how to hold both.

detail.abstract: Whether artificial intelligence pays off for the firms that build it into their products is hard to establish, because AI innovation is itself hard to observe. The medical technology sector is a rare exception: an AI-enabled device must obtain clearance from a national health authority before it can reach a patient, leaving a dated, firm-attributable record of AI innovation output that can be observed directly rather than proxied. We exploit this setting with a three-stage recursive model estimated on a novel firm-level dataset linking FDA premarket clearances, USPTO patents, Scopus publications, and Orbis financials, tracing the full innovation chain from external collaboration through AI device introduction to firm performance. We find that external AI research collaboration is a robust driver of AI device introduction across firm sizes and estimators, with a larger effect for small firms, consistent with external knowledge ties substituting for limited internal R&D capacity. Decomposing by partner type, the effect is largest for industry and clinical collaborations and smallest for academic ties, consistent with the former being closer to the regulatory and commercialisation process. Firms that bring AI devices to market display higher labour productivity-an effect robust for small firms and the full sample that holds under both sequential and joint maximum-likelihood estimation and accumulates across successive device introductions. Effects on profit margins are present but weaker and do not survive all specifications, a pattern consistent with competitive entry eroding pricing power as AI devices diffuse through the sector.

detail.abstract: This study evaluates global commercial insurance and reinsurance market stability entering 2026 using the Risk Resilience Factor for Insurance (RRF-i)—a proprietary metric integrating macroeconomic variables (60% weight) and political risk drivers (40% weight) across more than 150 sovereign jurisdictions. detail.abstract: Using a large dataset of countries during the last forty years, this paper analyzes the main determinants of export diversification. We explore the role of several factors and we use three different indicators of export diversification. We find robust evidence across specifications and indicators that trade openness induces higher specialization and does not favor export diversification. In contrast, financial development helps countries to diversify their exports. Looking at the effects of exchange rates, our results suggest a negative effect of real exchange rate overvaluation, but not significant effects of exchange rate volatility. We also find evidence that capital accumulation contributes positively to diversity exports and that increasing remoteness tend to reduce export diversification. We explore also the role of terms of trade shocks. Some of our results suggest that there is an interesting interaction between this variable and human capital. We find that improvements in terms of trade tend to concentrate exports, but this effect is lower for those countries with higher levels of human capital. This evidence suggests that countries with higher education can take advantage of positive terms of trade shocks to increase export diversification.

detail.abstract: Markets continuously update expectations about the Federal Reserve (Fed) policy prior to Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcements. Extending the standard event-study identification framework used on FOMC announcement days, we measure inferred Fed policy surprises on non-FOMC-days using the same market instruments and identification methodology. We show that cumulative inferred surprises between FOMC meetings explain a substantial portion of subsequent FOMC-day policy surprises, and can be used to predict interest rate and foreign exchange (FX) movements on FOMC announcement days. Moreover, as price adjustments in certain FX and fixed income markets continue in the hours following a macroeconomic news announcement and into the next day, inferred surprises also help predict asset price movements following these news announcements.

detail.abstract: International commercial contracts commonly contain both governing-law and dispute-resolution clauses, yet the two are often treated as separate drafting decisions. This article examines the extent to which these clauses should instead be considered as interconnected choices. It argues that, although governing law and dispute resolution perform legally distinct functions, their interaction can significantly affect the operation of a contract once a dispute arises. This is particularly evident in international arbitration, where the substantive governing law may operate alongside the law of the arbitral seat, the law governing the arbitration agreement, and the law relevant to recognition and enforcement. The article argues for coordination rather than uniformity. Parties do not need to select the same jurisdiction for the governing law, forum, or arbitral seat. Instead, these choices should be assessed together to ensure that their combined legal and practical consequences are understood.

detail.abstract: We study an income-account channel of exchange-rate transmission using matched data on Japanese multinational parents and their foreign affiliates. During the sharp yen depreciation of 2021–22, we find that (i) foreign affiliates with greater exchange-rate exposure expanded their activity and generated more profits, with larger payments to their Japanese parents, and (ii) more exposed parents increased their average wages and shifted employment toward commercial branches and offices involved in sales, purchasing, and related business functions, with offsetting declines in other employment. A multinational firm model in which scarce parent-side support inputs are allocated between domestic operations and foreign affiliates rationalizes these findings. To study the aggregate implications, we embed this mechanism in a two-country general-equilibrium model with trade and multinational production. The model shows that moving foreign-market activity from exports to affiliate production reduces the domestic real GDP response to depreciation and shifts more of the external adjustment from trade and toward income earned abroad. Depreciation therefore need not generate a large expansion in domestic production.
